name: WidgetCalc — Pricing, Quote & Cost Calculators for Leads
author: rocksoftware

sections.description:
Most WordPress calculator plugins either need you to write formulas in code, or lock lead capture behind an expensive plan. WidgetCalc is built the other way round: activate this plugin, drop the block or shortcode on any page with no setup at all, and you’ll see a real, working lead-capturing calculator straight away — it starts out showing widgetcalc.com’s own public demo calculator, no account, no signup. When you’re ready for your own, build a pricing calculator, quote calculator or cost estimator in a point-and-click editor at widgetcalc.com, publish it, and paste its key in to replace the demo — free plan included, no credit card.

Whatever you’re building it for — a pricing calculator that quotes a price from a visitor’s answers, a quote form for a service business, a cost estimator for a project, or an ROI/savings calculator for a landing page — a WidgetCalc calculator asks a visitor a few questions (spend, team size, hours spent per week — whatever your calculator needs), shows them a result worth sharing (“You could save €4,200/year” or “Your estimated quote: €1,250”), and captures their email before or after that result so every calculation becomes a lead in your dashboard, not just a number on the page.

Why WidgetCalc instead of a generic form plugin or a hand-coded script?

  • Works the moment you activate it. No key to find first: the block and shortcode show widgetcalc.com’s public demo calculator out of the box — no account needed — so you see a real one working on your site before you build anything.
  • No formulas to write. Build the calculator at widgetcalc.com with a visual editor — fields, a formula built by clicking, and a live preview — then paste one key here. Nothing to code on the WordPress side, ever.
  • The lead capture is built in. The calculator is the lead form; you don’t wire up a separate Contact Form 7 or Gravity Forms integration to get the email address.
  • A free plan that actually works. One calculator, unlimited visitors, no time limit — not a 14-day trial.
  • Light and lazy. The calculator loads in an iframe after the rest of your page, so it never blocks or slows down your WordPress site’s own load.

This plugin puts that calculator on a WordPress site with no code:

  • A [widgetcalc] shortcode you can drop into any page, post or widget area.
  • A WidgetCalc block for the block editor (Gutenberg), with a field for the calculator key.
  • A site-wide default calculator key under Settings → WidgetCalc, so a single-calculator site needs no attributes at all.

Build your calculator at widgetcalc.com first (a free plan covers one calculator), copy its key from the publish step, and paste it here.

Usage

  1. Activate the plugin, then add the WidgetCalc block or [widgetcalc] shortcode (no attributes needed) anywhere — it already shows a live, working demo calculator.
  2. When you’re ready for your own: create and publish a calculator at widgetcalc.com, copy the calculator key shown on the publish step (the part of the embed snippet between /embed/ and .js), and either:
    • Go to Settings → WidgetCalc and paste it as your default key to replace the demo everywhere, or
    • Use [widgetcalc key="your-calculator-key"] to place a specific calculator, independent of the default.

Does this need a paid WidgetCalc plan?

No. The plugin works with WidgetCalc’s free plan (one calculator, WidgetCalc badge shown). Paid plans add more calculators, remove the badge and unlock lead routing.

I don’t want to build the calculator myself — can WidgetCalc do it?

Yes. WidgetCalc also sells a done-for-you service: send your pricing sheet or formula and they build, publish and host the calculator for you, for a fixed one-time setup fee plus monthly hosting. It’s a separate paid service from this free plugin, not a requirement to use it — see the built-for-you offer and its Terms of Service. A link to it is also on this plugin’s own Settings → WidgetCalc page.

External services

This plugin loads your calculator from WidgetCalc, the hosted service it is
a shortcut for — it has no function without it.

  • What: a loader script, https://widgetcalc.com/embed/{your-calculator-key}.js,
    requested directly by the visitor’s browser for every page that shows a
    [widgetcalc] shortcode or WidgetCalc block.
  • When: on every page view where the shortcode or block is placed.
  • What data is sent: the calculator key you configured (part of the
    script URL) and the standard request data any script load sends (the
    visitor’s IP address and user agent, to the hosting server). The visitor’s
    own answers inside the calculator (and an email address, if the
    calculator asks for one) are sent to WidgetCalc only if the visitor fills
    in and submits the calculator; the plugin itself sends nothing on their
    behalf.
  • Provided by: Rock Software Oy, WidgetCalc — Terms of Service, Privacy Policy.

If you save a Pro licence key under Settings → WidgetCalc, the plugin also sends that key, once, to https://widgetcalc.com/pro/validate to confirm it is real; no other data leaves your site for this check.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the widgetcalc folder to /wp-content/plugins/, or install directly from the WordPress plugin directory.
  2. Activate the plugin through the Plugins menu in WordPress.
  3. Add the WidgetCalc block to any page, or use the [widgetcalc] shortcode — it shows a live demo calculator with no setup.
  4. When you’re ready for your own: go to Settings → WidgetCalc and paste your calculator’s key to replace the demo.
sections.faq:
Can I use this to build a quote form, not just a calculator?

Yes. A WidgetCalc “calculator” is really a questions-to-result flow — the same builder makes a pricing calculator, a quote form that ends in “your estimated price is…”, or a cost estimator for a project. Start from the price-quote template at widgetcalc.com if a quote form is what you need.

Is this a cost estimator plugin?

Yes, among other things. Templates for cost estimators, pricing calculators, ROI calculators and time/savings calculators are all built in the same visual editor and embed with the same shortcode or block — pick the template closest to what you need and edit it, no code.

Is this really free, or is lead capture locked behind a paid plan?

The free WidgetCalc plan includes one calculator, unlimited visitors and lead capture with no time limit — the thing most calculator plugins charge for. Paid plans add more calculators, remove the WidgetCalc badge and unlock lead routing (webhooks, more export options); they are not required to get real leads from this plugin.

Do I need to write a formula or any code?

No. You build the calculator itself at widgetcalc.com in a visual editor — add fields, build the formula by clicking them together, and see a live preview as you go — then paste the finished calculator’s key into this plugin. Nothing here needs code.

What does the plugin show before I set a key?

A real, working demo calculator from widgetcalc.com (no account needed), not a blank space or a placeholder message. It stays until you save your own calculator’s key under Settings → WidgetCalc, or pass a different key="…" to the shortcode.

Where do I get my own calculator key?

Create a calculator at widgetcalc.com (or start from a template) and publish it; the publish step shows an embed snippet, and the key is the UUID between /embed/ and .js in that snippet. Paste it under Settings → WidgetCalc to replace the demo everywhere, or use [widgetcalc key="…"] to place it on one specific page only.

Can I embed more than one calculator?

Yes — set a site-wide default under Settings → WidgetCalc for your main calculator, then use [widgetcalc key="…"] with a different key anywhere you want a different one.

Does this slow down my site?

The calculator loads in a lazy iframe, after the rest of your page, so it does not block your page’s own load.

Is there a paid licence for the plugin itself?

Optional. A one-time EUR 49 Pro licence (no subscription) removes the “Made with WidgetCalc” badge and lifts the free plan’s calculator and visitor limits on the WidgetCalc account you paste the key for — paste the key under Settings → WidgetCalc once you’ve bought one at widgetcalc.com/pro. The plugin works fully on the free plan without it.
sections.changelog:
1.0.11

  • Fixed: the block and shortcode rendered the calculator in the wrong place — at the very
    bottom of the page, after the theme’s footer — instead of where you put them in your
    content. The loader script now prints inline instead of being queued to load in the
    footer, so the calculator appears exactly where the block/shortcode is placed. Found by
    walking a clean install through Activate -> add the block -> view the front end as a
    visitor: the settings screen’s own demo never showed this, because it already printed its
    script inline; every real front-end use of the block/shortcode did not.

1.0.10

  • Settings → WidgetCalc has a new, optional “Pro licence key” field for the one-time EUR 49
    Pro licence (badge removal, no calculator/visitor limits): paste a key and the plugin
    confirms it with widgetcalc.com and shows whether it is active.
  • Close the activate -> nobody-ever-finds-the-demo leak: activating the plugin now opens
    Settings → WidgetCalc straight away, the one screen that already shows the live public
    demo and explains adding the block/shortcode. Before this, activation returned you to the
    plain Plugins list with no next step — confirmed on a clean install that nothing visible
    changes anywhere on the site until a block or shortcode is placed by hand, which is why
    374 downloads turned into fewer than 10 active installs.

1.0.8

  • Settings → WidgetCalc now shows the public demo calculator rendering live on the page
    itself, not just a link out to it — activating the plugin and opening that one screen is
    enough to see a real calculator working, with no separate page to create first.

1.0.7

  • Close the activate -> blank-page leak: the block and shortcode now default to
    widgetcalc.com’s own public demo calculator (no account needed) instead of showing
    nothing until you build and paste your own key. Settings → WidgetCalc explains this
    plainly instead of blocking on an empty key.
  • Fix a dead link: the listing’s description and FAQ pointed at
    widgetcalc.com/calculators (plural), which requires a login — not the public,
    no-account demo pages. Every link now goes to a page that actually works without
    signing in.

1.0.6

  • Sell the no-signup path first: the listing’s short description, intro and two FAQ entries now
    lead with copying a ready-made calculator’s embed key straight from widgetcalc.com/calculators
    — no account — before asking anyone to build their own. Those three calculators’ public pages
    and keys shipped on widgetcalc.com itself this week; this release is the listing catching up
    to say so.

1.0.5

  • Add a FAQ entry and a settings-page link for the “built-for-you” done-for-you service
    (send your pricing sheet, WidgetCalc builds and hosts the calculator) — a separate paid
    service from this free plugin, linked only from the plugin’s own settings screen, not from
    any front-facing page it renders.

1.0.4

  • Retitle the listing and rewrite the tags, description and two new FAQ entries around the
    words a WordPress site owner actually searches for (pricing calculator, quote form, cost
    estimator), not just “ROI widget” — the plugin always did all of these, the listing just
    didn’t say so.

1.0.3

  • Add the directory listing’s first screenshots: a live calculator, the builder with its live
    preview, and the embed snippet — so a visitor can see the product work before installing.

1.0.2

  • Rewrite the directory listing as a landing page: a sharper title, a “why WidgetCalc” section in the description, and two new FAQ entries (is it really free, do I need to code) answering the two questions a visitor to this listing actually has.
  • The admin settings screen now shows a plain “Build a free calculator” button when no key is set yet, linking through a counted redirect so we can see whether an install turns into a signup.

1.0.1

  • Fix: enqueue the embed loader via wp_enqueue_script instead of printing a raw
  • Document the WidgetCalc external service (data sent, ToS, privacy) in this readme.
  • Remove an unsupported “fastest” claim from the description; add rocksoftware as a listed contributor.

1.0.0

  • First release: shortcode, block and a site-wide default key.
